la:verb:vio.html:
vĭo, āre, v. n.
via
,
to go, travel (postAug. and very rare; cf.: vio pro eo infelicius fictum,): legati intenti ad viandum,: iter viandi multifidum,: vians maritus,travelling about,; , p. 184; ; ; .—P. a. as subst.: vĭantes, ium, m., travellers: viantibus opportunae viae,.

la:verb:violo.gloss: to treat with violence; to maltreat
senses: to treat with violence; to maltreat
la:verb:violo.html:
vĭŏlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
vis
,
to treat with violence (corporeally, and, more freq., mentally), to injure, dishonor, outrage, violate (cf.: laedo, polluo, contamino).
Lit. with persons as objects: hospites violare fas non putant,to injure, do violence to,: aliquem,: patriam prodere, parentes violare,.—Esp.: virginem, Auct. ap. Müll.; ; cf. : sacrum vulnere corpus,; cf.: Getico peream violatus ab arcu,.—
Transf.
With places as objects, to invade, violate, profane: fines eorum se violaturum negavit,: loca religiosa et lucos,: Iliacos agros ferro,: Cereale nemus securi,: silva vetus nullāque diu violata securi,.—
With the senses as objects, to outrage, shock: oculos nostros (tua epistola),; cf.: aures meas obsceno sermone,.—
With abstract objects, to violate, outrage, break, injure, etc.: officium,: jus,: religionem,: virginitatem alicujus,: vitam patris,: inducias per scelus,to break,: foedera,; : amicitiam,: existimationem absentis,; cf.: nominis nostri famam tuis probris,: dignitatem alicujus in aliquā re,; cf.: injuriae sunt, quae aut pulsatione corpus aut convicio aures aut aliquā turpitudine vitam cujuspiam violant,.—
Trop. (rare and poet.): Indum sanguineo ostro ebur,i. e. to dye of a blood-red, (an imitation of the Homeric ἐλέφαντα φοίνικι μιήνη, Il. 4, 141).

la:adj:violabilis.html:
vĭŏlābĭlis, e, adj.
violo
,
that may be injured or violated, violable (poet.): cor levibus telis,: non violabile numen,: turba nullis armis, senes,.

la:adj:violentus.html:
vĭŏlentus, a, um, adj.
vis
,
forcible, violent, vehement, impetuous, boisterous (class.): ubi id rescivit factum frater violentissimus,: homo vehemens et violentus,: quamvis sis, ut es, violentus et furens,: tyrannus saevissimus et violentissimus in suos,: censores,: ingenium,; cf.: Piso ingenio violentus,: faciē violenta Corinna est,: violentus in armis,: viri vis,: vis leonum,: Lucania bellum Incuteret violenta,: ventus,: turbo,; ; : violentior Eurus,: violentior amnis,: violentissimae tempestates,: violentissimus caeli status,: duae res violentissimae, ferrum et ignis,: opes,: verba,: imperium,: mors infantibus,: nimis violentum est, nulla esse dicere,i. e. it is unreasonable, it is going too far,.—Adv. does not occur.

la:noun:viola.html:
vĭŏla, ae, f.dim.
Gr. ἴον
,
the violet, the stock-gillyflower.
Lit., ; ; ; . —Collect.: an tu me in violā putabas aut in rosā dicere?—
A violet color, violet, ; ; ; .

la:noun:violentia.html:
vĭŏlentĭa, ae, f.
violentus
,
violence, vehemence, impetuosity, ferocity (class.): illi hanc vim appellant, quae est potius violentia,: novi hominis furorem, novi effrenatam violentiam,: vinolentorum,: minis ejus ac violentiā territus, 34: gentium,ferocity,: acris leonum,.—Of things, concr. and abstr.: vehemens vini,: saepe fortunae violentiam toleravisse,: assidua hiemis,: radii solis,: vultūs,fierceness,: si dolo nihil profecerit, vi et violentiā deicere eos conatur,.

la:adj:violens.html:
vĭŏlens, entis, adj.
vis
,
impetuous, vehement, furious, violent (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose, whereas violentus is class.): Aufidus,: victor equus,; so (with ferus),.

la:noun:violator.html:
vĭŏlātor, ōris, m.
id.
,
an injurer, profaner, violator (not in Cic. or Cæs.): templi,: juris gentium,: foederis,: dictatoris (C. Caesaris),i. e. murderer,—In apposit., fem.: natrix violator aquae,i. e. polluting, poisoning,.

la:adv:violenter.html:
vĭŏlenter, adv.
violens
,
impetuously, vehemently, violently: solennia ludorum violenter dirimere. : quaestio exercita aspere violenterque,furiously,; cf.: aliquid tolerare,: vidimus flavum Tiberim retortis Litore Etrusco violenter undis Ire dejectum monumenta regis,: invadunt appropinquantem (canes),: proconsulatum violenter gerere,: aliquem ad supplicium poscere,: increpare aliquem,.—Comp., ; ; ; .—Sup., ; .
